Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

imfeatures 0.1.0 (development)

Spatial pooling: documentation, a new vignette, and three fixes

Convolutional feature maps can be reduced over space in several ways: global average or max, a coarse grid, low-frequency DCT modes, centre-to-periphery rings, or not at all. These options are now documented in one place.

  • New vignette, vignette("spatial-pooling"). It shows what each option keeps, how wide the resulting VGG-16 features are, and how the string options ("avg", "max", "none", "resize_HxW") relate to the pooler objects (global_average_pool(), adaptive_grid_pool(), dct_pool(), radial_pool(), identity_pool()). It runs without Keras or Python.
  • New help page ?poolers compares the pooler objects. The help for each pooler, pool_activations(), pooler_feature_names(), vgg_hierarchy_spec(), vgg16_block_end_spec(), extract_features() and extract_vgg_features() now states output sizes, column order and scale, with examples.
  • Printing a vgg_hierarchy_spec now lists the pooler of each stage.
  • All vignettes and the pkgdown site now use the albersdown theme from CRAN (albersdown::albers_vignette, red family, homage preset).

Fixes:

  • adaptive_grid_pool() failed with “invalid number of intervals” when either grid dimension was 1, for example adaptive_grid_pool(1, 3). A single bin now works; adaptive_grid_pool(1, 1) equals global average pooling. Results for two or more bins are unchanged.
  • radial_pool() accepted breaks outside [0, 1] and silently returned all-zero columns for the rings they defined. Such breaks are now an error. A ring that holds no positions on a small map still gives zeros, now with a warning.
  • extract_vgg_features(pooling = ) accepted only "resize_3x3", "resize_5x5" and "resize_7x7", while extract_features() accepted any "resize_HxW". Both now accept any positive H and W, and both reject a zero size such as "resize_0x3" up front.

One naming change: when extract_feature_hierarchy() flattens a convolutional map with identity_pool(), columns are now named by channel and position (b5::channel_001::y1_x1) instead of by index (b5::f_001). When a dense stage is given a spatial pooler, its columns are named fc1::f_001, as they pass through unpooled. Values and column order are unchanged in both cases.

One thing to know: dct_pool() returns the spatial mean as its first column, but its other columns grow with the size of the map (16 times larger at 224 x 224 than at 14 x 14 for the same pattern). This has not changed. Standardize DCT columns before combining them; block_pca() does so by default.

Edge entropy: image-frame artifact and new boundary option

What was wrong. Edge entropy filters each image with 31 x 31 Gabor filters. Pixels outside the image were treated as zero (black), so the image frame looked like a strong, perfectly straight edge at 0 and 90 degrees. Only a 2-pixel border of filter responses was discarded, but the frame response reaches 3-4 pixels into the image (about 35% of the border brightness at pixel 3). Those responses can enter the strongest-edge set used for the pairwise statistics. Both backends (use_cpp = TRUE and FALSE) behaved this way. Shikang raised the concern.

Who is affected.

  • Full-frame natural photographs: changes are small. On 17 test photographs, rank correlations between the old and corrected features were 0.99 or higher.
  • Objects on plain or uniform backgrounds, or images with large flat regions: changes can be large. Frame responses made up 7-20% of the retained edges. Rank correlations for pentropy_160_240 fell to 0.15-0.79, with shifts of up to 1.7 bits. Some long-range values exist only because of the frame and become NA once it is removed.
  • Whole-image versus foreground comparisons (for example with compute_saliency_features()): only the whole image includes the frame edges, so part of any difference can be the artifact.

What changed. compute_edge_entropy() and compute_saliency_features() gain boundary = c("zero", "reflect"). "reflect" mirrors the image across its edges before filtering, so the frame creates no edge. Responses more than 15 pixels from the edge are unchanged. The default stays "zero", so existing scripts reproduce earlier results exactly. Use "reflect" for new analyses.

How to run it.

# Install this version
remotes::install_github("bbuchsbaum/imfeatures", ref = "claude/gallant-meitner-a4r2x3")
library(imfeatures)

compute_edge_entropy("stim/img001.jpg", boundary = "reflect")
compute_saliency_features("stim/img001.jpg", sal_map, "weights", boundary = "reflect")

How to tell whether your results change. Compute the features both ways on your actual stimuli and compare.

files <- list.files("stim", pattern = "\\.(jpe?g|png)$", full.names = TRUE)
feats <- c("entropy", "pentropy_20_80", "pentropy_80_160",
           "pentropy_160_240", "complex_before")
old <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files, compute_edge_entropy, boundary = "zero"))
new <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files, compute_edge_entropy, boundary = "reflect"))

# 1. Do image rankings change? Spearman rho near 1 means the same order.
sapply(feats, function(f) cor(old[[f]], new[[f]], method = "spearman",
                              use = "complete.obs"))

# 2. How big are the changes, relative to the spread across images?
sapply(feats, function(f) {
  d <- new[[f]] - old[[f]]
  c(mean_diff = mean(d, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_abs_diff = max(abs(d), na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_across_images = sd(old[[f]], na.rm = TRUE))
})

# 3. Which values only existed because of the frame?
sapply(feats, function(f) sum(!is.na(old[[f]]) & is.na(new[[f]])))

# 4. Which images moved most? Look at these first.
d <- abs(new$pentropy_160_240 - old$pentropy_160_240)
head(old$im[order(d, decreasing = TRUE)], 10)

How to read the comparison:

  • If every Spearman rho is about 0.98 or higher, and the largest change is small next to the spread across images, the artifact is unlikely to matter. Still rerun the main models once to confirm.
  • With few images (under about 20), rho can drop because of very small changes that happen to swap close neighbours. In that case judge mainly by max_abs_diff against sd_across_images.
  • If rho is lower for any feature, or values become NA, rerun the downstream analyses with "reflect" features and compare the effect sizes and conclusions, not only whether results stay significant. Long distance ranges such as pentropy_160_240 are the most likely to change.
  • For whole-image versus foreground hypotheses, compute both measures with boundary = "reflect" before interpreting the difference.
  • To report results either way, state which boundary setting was used. compute_saliency_features() records it in metadata$filter$boundary.

Other changes

  • Fix compute_feature_similarity() with lowmem = TRUE (the default). It read the image-path column of extract_features() output instead of the features, so off-diagonal similarities were NA, and it left the diagonal at 0. It now matches lowmem = FALSE.
  • Use OpenCLIP validation preprocessing in clip_features() instead of random training augmentation when extracting image features (#51).
  • Recompute affected file-input edge entropy analyses: file paths passed to compute_edge_entropy() with use_cpp = TRUE (the default) were flattened into one column by an array-to-matrix conversion. Both spatial dimensions are now preserved. Previous results from that path are unreliable; matrix inputs were unaffected by this conversion defect.
  • Add compute_saliency_features() for saliency-weighted first-order and pairwise edge entropy, with selected-edge mean normalization, support diagnostics, centre-bias controls, exact map transformations, and donor maps.
  • Add saliency_location_entropy(), saliency_multiscale_entropy(), and reproducible saliency_donor_assignments(). Map representation is explicit; zero mass remains distinct from a valid entropy of zero.
  • Correct native edge entropy to return NA for zero histogram mass, matching R. Defined matrix-input legacy outputs and the existing result layout are preserved.
  • Count saliency controls sharing an edge set in one geometry pass, and reuse baseline counts and support statistics. Both new backends use Euclidean geometry and the native legacy validity rule. Historical R conventions remain confined to compute_edge_entropy(use_cpp = FALSE).
  • Add common-support pairwise contrasts, separate means for distinct transform and donor controls, and an optional entropy-matched Gaussian centre control. Unweighted contrasts describe the overall effect of weighting; matched comparisons help distinguish spatial alignment from concentration effects.
  • Average probability maps when downsampling, record observed and donor concentration before/after resizing, and allow a declared small donor aspect-ratio tolerance. Add a runnable saliency vignette and localization, backend-parity, common-support, and realistic-size regression tests.
